title: How solar panels make electricity
examples: Do solar panels only work when it is sunny outside?
What is the difference between the electricity they make and the electricity in our homes?
Are solar panels efficient? How much power do they make?

explain.say: Today we are learning how solar panels create electricity.
First we look at photovoltaic cells which are the main parts.
These cells often use silicon which is a key material for them.
When sunlight hits the panel photons are the energy packets we need.
These photons knock loose free electrons starting the flow of power.
The electricity generated by panels is direct current or direct current.

faq.q: Do solar panels only work when it is sunny outside?
faq.a: They work best in bright sunlight, but they can still generate some power on cloudy days. You might also need some direct sunlight to make them work well.

faq.q: What is the difference between the electricity they make and the electricity in our homes?
faq.a: Solar panels create direct current or DC electricity. Most household appliances use alternating current or AC electricity, so an inverter changes it.
asks: Is DC the same as AC?
Why do I need an inverter?

faq.q: How does the silicon material help with this process?
faq.a: Silicon is a semiconductor, meaning it can conduct electricity under certain conditions. This property is what makes it perfect for collecting the energy from photons.

faq.q: What is a photon, and how does it relate to solar power?
faq.a: A photon is a particle of light energy. When a photon hits the solar cell, it transfers enough energy to knock electrons loose, starting the electrical current.
asks: Are photons like tiny bullets of light?

faq.q: What is direct current, and why is it important for solar power?
faq.a: Direct current means the electrical charge flows in only one direction. Solar panels naturally produce this direct current type of electricity.

facts: Photovoltaic cells convert light energy directly into electrical energy.
Silicon is the most common semiconductor material used in solar panels.
Sunlight is composed of packets of energy called photons.
The electricity produced by solar panels is direct current or DC.

quiz.say: What type of energy do photons carry when they strike a solar cell?
quiz.why: Photons are defined as packets of light energy, which is what starts the process.

wrong.0: Heat is energy, but photons carry the light energy that initiates the electron release.
wrong.1: Chemical potential is related to bonds, not the direct energy from light waves.
wrong.2: While electrons have kinetic energy, the initial input from light is the photon's energy.

quiz.say: If a solar panel is made of silicon, what property allows it to generate electricity?
quiz.why: Silicon is a semiconductor, meaning it can conduct electricity when energy is applied to it.

wrong.1: While it conducts, 'semiconductor' is the more precise term describing its ability to conduct under certain conditions.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because if it resisted all flow, no electricity would be made.
wrong.3: An insulator blocks electricity, which is the opposite of what the panel needs to do.

quiz.say: The flow of electricity from a solar panel is best described as:
quiz.why: Solar panels naturally produce a steady flow of electricity in one direction, which is direct current.

wrong.0: The flow is systematic and predictable, not random.
wrong.1: A static charge is stored energy, not the continuous flow of electricity needed to power things.
wrong.3: AC changes direction regularly, which is what household wiring typically uses, but not what the panel makes.
